title: Generalizing Graph Foundation Models via Hyperbolic Retrieval-Augmented Generation

problem.claim: Graph foundation models have insufficient parameterized knowledge to cope with distribution shifts, limiting their generalization ability.

gap.claim: Existing Euclidean-space retrieval-augmented generation frameworks are geometrically mismatched with tree-structured external knowledge bases, causing loss of semantic granularity and hubness.

contributions.claim: A Hyperbolic Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework is proposed to enhance graph foundation model generalization.
A Hyperbolic Knowledge Indexing module models external knowledge-base hierarchies in hyperbolic space.
Multi-granularity Retrieval and Dual-path Fusion provide coarse- and fine-grained knowledge retrieval and integrate knowledge at feature and structural levels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple graph benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements in the zero-shot setting.
The reported results highlight generalization for robust graph foundation model inference.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph foundation models use large-scale pre-training for cross-domain graph inference.
Their parameterized knowledge is insufficient under distribution shifts, limiting generalization.
Euclidean retrieval-augmented generation is poorly matched to tree-structured external knowledge and can lose semantic granularity while producing hubness.
HyRAG uses hyperbolic indexing, multi-granularity retrieval, and dual-path fusion to integrate external knowledge.
The authors report significant zero-shot improvements on multiple graph benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Tree-structured external knowledge is described as mismatched with Euclidean geometry.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval geometry may affect preservation of semantic hierarchy and granularity.

application.claim: For hierarchical external knowledge, consider representations whose geometry reflects tree-like structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether hyperbolic geometry is beneficial beyond the reported benchmarks and setting.

unknowns: Benchmark identities, dataset sizes, baselines, metrics, and improvement magnitudes are not specified.
The abstract does not describe training procedures, computational costs, or ablations.
The distribution shifts and graph tasks evaluated are not specified.
